items.stem: Which condition is most important to test on mobile that is often overlooked on desktop web?

options.text: Behaviour when connectivity drops and later recovers
options.rationale: Correct: mobile networks are variable, so loss and recovery of connectivity is a core scenario.
Hover is a desktop concern, not a mobile priority.
Print preview is rarely relevant to a mobile app.
Desktop tiling is not a mobile scenario.

items.explanation: Correct: intermittent connectivity and recovery is a defining mobile condition to verify.

items.stem: Which TWO interruptions should a mobile test suite verify do not corrupt an in-progress transaction? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: a call backgrounds the app and must not corrupt state.

options.text: The OS revoking a permission while backgrounded
options.rationale: Correct: permission changes while backgrounded can break resumed flows.

options.text: The user changing the device wallpaper
options.rationale: Changing wallpaper does not affect app transaction state.
Icon layout changes are unrelated to in-app transactions.

items.explanation: Correct: calls and permission changes while backgrounded are real interruptions that can corrupt state.

items.stem: For a large, fragmented Android user base, how should a coverage matrix be chosen?

options.text: By prioritising device/OS combinations that match real usage data
options.rationale: Correct: coverage should follow actual user device and OS distribution.

options.text: By testing only the newest OS version
options.rationale: Many users run older OS versions that must be covered.

options.text: By testing only one emulator configuration
options.rationale: A single emulator cannot represent fragmentation.

options.text: By testing every possible device that exists
options.rationale: Exhaustive device coverage is infeasible; usage-based prioritisation is used.

items.explanation: Correct: a coverage matrix is prioritised by real-world usage data, not newest-only or exhaustive testing.
